items.claim: The Isa.24.21-23 boundary is warranted: the ba-yom-hahu onset that opens the span and the enthronement acclamation that closes it both collate at byte tier, and the marked petuchah/setumah brackets at the span's outer edges are the only span-relevant marks in range.
items.evidence: The Hebrew forms cited for the opening, “It will happen in that day…” via web:Isa.24.21, and the closing enthronement line, “Yahweh of Armies will reign…” via web:Isa.24.23, both collate at byte tier against the Masoretic verses they cite. The setumah before the span (after Isa.24.20) and the petuchah at its close (after Isa.24.23) are the only parashah marks touching Isa.24.20-24.23, so the disclosure is complete, and no undisclosed title chain, refrain, or oracle header from elsewhere in the book crosses this seam.

items.claim: The Isa.25.1-5 hymn boundary is warranted by an objective addressee shift: second-person address to Yahweh runs through Isa.25.5 and gives way to third-person narration at Isa.25.6, matching a petuchah bracket on both outer edges of the span.
items.evidence: The opening line's Hebrew collates at byte tier. The WEB text keeps second-person forms addressed to Yahweh through Isa.25.5 (“you will bring down the noise of strangers”), while Isa.25.6 switches to third-person (“Yahweh of Armies will make…”) — an objective, checkable seam. The petuchah marks after Isa.24.23 and after Isa.25.5 are the only parashah marks bracketing the span, both correctly disclosed.

items.claim: The Isa.25.6-8 boundary is warranted: third-person mountain-banquet narration runs to its climactic line at Isa.25.8, a fresh reported-speech formula opens a distinct confession at Isa.25.9, and petuchah marks correctly bracket both edges.
items.evidence: Both cited Hebrew forms (the mountain phrase at the opening and the death-swallowed line at the close) collate at byte tier. Isa.25.9 opens with its own “it shall be said” formula rather than continuing this unit's third-person description, and the petuchah after Isa.25.5 and after Isa.25.8 are the only parashah marks touching the span.

items.claim: The applied unit_type is given to a projected communal confession without the one-sentence deviation disclosure the operative-category rule requires when a category is used outside its named examples.
items.evidence: Isa.25.9's content (“Behold, this is our God!… We will be glad and rejoice in his salvation!”) is the people's own retrospective acclamation of an already-accomplished rescue, not a promise or comfort oracle spoken outward by a divine or prophetic voice, so it does not obviously fit the applied category's promise/comfort description. The closed vocabulary's sung-praise alternative is at least as plausible a fit for this brief doxological outburst introduced by its own quotation formula, and no deviation sentence is supplied arguing the choice either way.

items.claim: The row's own notes name the shared staged verification apparatus directly ("per the toolkit's fold guidance"), a barred staged-file reference in row prose, even though the underlying fold-versus-content reasoning for the boundary is itself sound.
items.evidence: The span's device notes state the WEB continuation-paragraph fold linking Isa.25.9 and Isa.25.10 is disclosed "per the toolkit's fold guidance" — naming the shared staged tooling rather than arguing the point from the bytes and the fold disclosure alone. The fold itself is correctly identified as tier-4 layout (a continuation-paragraph fold at Isa.25.10, confirmed against the staged verse map), and the content pivot to Moab at Isa.25.10 is a genuine, checkable seam, so the boundary call is not in question — only the register violation in its own notes.

items.claim: The Isa.26.1-6 song boundary is warranted directly by WEB's own quotation punctuation, which opens at Isa.26.1 and closes at Isa.26.6 with no further quotation marks resuming before Isa.27.2, and the short-Yah-form count cited for Isa.26.4 is accurate.
items.evidence: No quotation punctuation appears anywhere from Isa.26.7 through Isa.26.21 in the staged WEB text, confirming that the quoted song's own closing mark at Isa.26.6 is the next punctuation signal after Isa.26.1's opening. The cited count of three book-wide short-Yah sites is accurate, and no parashah mark falls inside Isa.26.1-6 to contest the span.

items.claim: The row quotes web:Isa.26.20 as its own close-boundary evidence without disclosing that the underlying Masoretic verse is ketiv/qere-bearing.
items.evidence: Isa.26.20 carries two ketiv/qere notes (single-witness) in the Masoretic apparatus. This row cites the verse's opening clause (“Come, my people, enter into your rooms”) as the signal for its own closing seam but supplies no ketiv/qere disclosure for that verse. The gap does not disturb the boundary placement itself, which rests on a genuine reversal of address at Isa.26.20 (second-person petition of the community to Yahweh giving way to an imperative addressed to the community), but the ketiv/qere status was available in the same staged inventory this row already draws its parashah citations from.

items.claim: The Isa.26.20-21 boundary is warranted by a genuine reversal of address (an imperative commanding the community rather than the community's own petition), and both ketiv/qere notes at Isa.26.20 and the setumah brackets at both edges are disclosed accurately.
items.evidence: Both cited Hebrew forms collate at byte tier. The two ketiv/qere notes on Isa.26.20 and the setumah marks after Isa.26.19 and after Isa.26.21 in the Masoretic inventory match the row's own disclosures exactly, and no undisclosed mark falls inside the two-verse span.
